title: Toxicity in Online Platforms and AI Systems: A Survey of Needs, Challenges, Mitigations, and Future Directions

bias_targets.methodology: Surveying literature that analyzes incivility rates in politically aligned forums (e.g., Reddit) and evaluating studies that administer political orientation assessments to LLMs (e.g., ChatGPT) to detect left-leaning or right-leaning tendencies.

Reviewing research and datasets focused on online misogyny, as well as evaluating how LLMs reinforce exclusionary language norms (e.g., excluding non-binary identities) and proxy variables in automated systems.

Surveying empirical studies and datasets (e.g., Social Bias Inference Corpus, RedditBias) that detect stereotyping, representation harms, and discriminatory content embedded within LLM training data and generated responses.
Evaluating specific experiments and mitigation techniques in the literature (e.g., Schafer et al.) that test for identity term bias focused on religious groups during toxicity detection.

Reviewing metrics, benchmarks, and explainable AI (XAI) techniques (e.g., attribution scores, LangFair, HateCheck) to evaluate how automated moderation and recommendation systems disproportionately disadvantage certain demographic groups.
